gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Notebookcheck's lab found the Galaxy Watch 8 LTE battery 'won't last for a whole day' when used for long periods without a connected phone (versus 24 h with AOD while connected), or that Apple's 18-hour rating for the SE 3 GPS + Cellular assumes only 4 of those hours on cellular.
standout_why: I read the two cited rival pages. Apple's support page (support.apple.com/en-us/119601) says only 'Turning on cellular for extended periods uses more battery power' and gives no figures. Samsung CA's setup page has no battery figures at all and says Galaxy Watch4 and later need a compatible phone for first setup. The uncited results ChatGPT got (Apple's kids-setup guides, Verizon, T-Mobile) are setup instructions. None of these pages has a measurement from a named reviewer, and none quantifies battery life away from the phone, which is the cost of the use this question is about.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Every cellular candidate is a one-day watch once it is really away from the phone. Notebookcheck measured that the Galaxy Watch 8 LTE does not last a full day of extended phone-free use. Apple's own 18 h SE 3 figure includes only 4 h on cellular, and the5krunner says the Pixel Watch 4's battery life 'shortens considerably with LTE usage'. The page should tell shoppers to expect a daily charge if they leave the phone at home, and it should treat the maker battery column as figures for use with the phone nearby. One caveat: Notebookcheck tested the 44 mm Galaxy Watch 8 (435 mAh), and we list the 40 mm. The page's battery cell should say which size was tested.
